sentences.text:
This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is arising out of award dated 21.04.2023 passed by Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jawad, District Neemuch (MP) in Claim Case No.40/2017 on account of exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability and setting aside of the impugned order.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jawad, District Neemuch
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (2) The brief facts of the case is that on 17.11.2015, deceased Jankidas Bairagi along with his son Shantilal going towards Motipura from Benganpura, Jawad, District Neemuch (MP).

He was going on bicycle, his son was coming on foot when the driver of motorcycle bearing registration number MP44MK-8184 driving it rashly and negligently dashed him due to which Jankidas Bairagi sustained grievous injuries and died.

(3) That the claimant/respondent No.1 and 2 filed a claim application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against the appellant and rest of the respondents, before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jawad, District Neemuch (MP) for compensation to deceased on account said vehicle accident.

(4) The appellant and the respondents No.3 and 4 have filed their written statement before the Tribunal and the Tribunal has framed the issue and after taking the evidence has awarded Rs.3,41,000/- in favour of the claimants from filing of claim application till its realization.

(5) Counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the ground that the Tribunal has committed error in not considering that in the FIR Ex.P/2 the number of offending vehicle was not mentioned and the criminal court has acquitted the driver of the offending vehicle and the Investigator of the Insurance Company had taken the statement of owner and driver of offending vehicle but they have denied the accident, so it is a clear cut case of false implication of the vehicle for seeking compensation.
(6) On the other hand, counsel for the respondents has supported the impugn award and prays for rejection of the appeal.
(7) I have heard counsel for both the parties and have perused the record of Tribunal with due care.
(8) After hearing counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it appears that the FIR was lodged on the same date of accident i.e. on 07.11.2015 in which it was mentioned that the accident has been caused by motorcycle Hero Honda Passion bearing registration no.MP44MK-8184 and the same was riding by Akram Hussain.

Thereafter the police investigated the matter and has seized the Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Bherubai on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167413797/
2 motorcycle/offending vehicle bearing registration no.MP44MK-8184 and after investigation, the police has filed the chargesheet before the Magistrate Court, Neemuch (MP) against the driver of offending vehicle.

entities.text: Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Bherubai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (9) It is settled law that if police files the chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle then the Tribunal presumes that the driver of offending vehicle held guilty and this is rebuttal presumption.

It is the duty of the party who stated that the accident had not occurred by the offending vehicle,
rebutted it by way of direct evidence or in evidence adduced by claimant.
(10) In the present case, the owner and driver of the offending vehicle was present before the Tribunal but they have not dared to enter into the witness box before the Tribunal.

(11) Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has submitted that the driver of offending vehicle was acquitted from the charge by the Magistrate Court but it is settled law that a claim case shall be decided by his own evidence and not on the basis of criminal record.

In the case of Raju Yadav vs.
Imrat Singh reported in 2002 Vol.-2 MPLN SN 24 the Coordinate Bench of this Court has held that acquitted the accused in the criminal trial does not resolve from the liability of compensation.

entities.text:
Raju Yadav vs.
Imrat Singh reported in 2002 Vol.-2 MPLN SN 24
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of RP Gautam vs RNM Singh and Another reported in AIR 2008 MP 68 the Coordinate Bench of this Court has held that it is settled proposition of law that every civil case is decided on it's own facts and evidence without influencing the papers and decision of the criminal case.

entities.text: RP Gautam vs RNM Singh and Another reported in AIR 2008 MP 68
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (12) Counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company has further submitted that the Investigator of Insurance Company has taken the evidence of owner and driver and they denied accident but they have not dared to enter into the witness box before the Tribunal, so the statement taken by him does not help or assist the Insurance Company.

(13) In view of the aforesaid and in the considered opinion of this court, the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the offending vehicle is held liable for the accident and hence the award passed by the Tribunal is affirmed.
Hence, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company sans merit and has no substance.
Accordingly, the same is dismissed.
